title: The cat slow blink
hook: Narrow your eyes slowly at a cat, and it may well do the same back.
peek: A slow, half-closed blink is one of the friendliest things a cat can do. A 2020 study found that cats often return the gesture when people do it first, and warm up to strangers who try it.
lede: Cat owners have long noticed that a relaxed cat will look at them, half close its eyes and blink slowly. Behaviourists call it the slow blink, and some nickname it the cat smile. In 2020, psychologists at the Universities of Sussex and Portsmouth tested it properly and found that cats really do answer a human slow blink with one of their own.

bullets.text: Tasmin Humphrey, Karen McComb and colleagues had owners slow-blink at their cats at home. The cats blinked back more often than when the owners sat with a neutral face. The work appeared in the journal Scientific Reports.
In a second experiment, a researcher the cats had never met tried it. Cats were more likely to approach her hand after she slow-blinked than after she kept a neutral expression.
Among cats, a fixed, unbroken stare can signal a challenge. The researchers suggest the slow blink may have begun as a way of interrupting that stare, softening the eyes to show no threat is meant.
The study describes it as a series of half blinks followed by a long narrowing or closing of the eyes. Try it from across the room, without staring, and give the cat time to answer.
